name: Consulting

claims.claim_text: A consulting firm working roughly ten concurrent projects lacks the slack to train a graduate engineer, so hiring favours established experts who can be productive immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: in a consulting firm, you do really want an expert. You want someone established.
claims.episode_title: Design & Manufacturing Consulting with Scott Williams from Xentronics

claims.claim_text: Self-employment in consulting does not automatically reduce working hours; consultants who set their own schedule frequently end up working 80-hour weeks.
claims.quote_verbatim: these people who go out there and do consulting gigs and think it's great that they're working for themselves, but they're actually working 80-hour weeks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The IEEE operates consultant networks that provide a formal support and networking structure for independent engineering consultants.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had some people asking on Twitter about support networks for consulting. And I actually didn't know of any. And it turns out, though, that IEEE has one.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer - Exhilarating ESC Escapades

claims.claim_text: Consultants working to a deadline commonly shut off social media clients and their pop-up notifications entirely during billable concentration work, because the interruption cost and the temptation to check both eat into deliverable time.
claims.quote_verbatim: If I'm doing my consulting and I need to concentrate, I need to get something out in a hurry, I will turn off Twitter
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Billable hours are a fraction of hours worked: fifty hours spent on a project may yield only twenty to thirty billable hours, and that gap must be priced into the rate along with holidays and unbilled gaps between engagements.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're working 50 hours on a project, you may only be able to bill 30 of those hours or even 20.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consulting rates track local cost of living, so quoted rates from high-cost regions such as California run substantially above those elsewhere, which surprises clients who have only benchmarked against salaries.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was very shocked when I saw people's rates and even more shocked when I saw people's rates in California, you know, like, just because it's a higher cost of living.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Undercutting pressure in consulting is a direct function of substitutability: a task a hundred other consultants can do equally well invites a price war, whereas specialisation and being wanted in particular insulate the rate.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're just doing something that, well, a hundred other consultants can do just as well, then you're often, you know, you're into that undercutting war
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A widely circulated consulting essay advises against quoting whole jobs where an hourly arrangement is possible, on the grounds that a whole-job quote places all schedule and technical risk on the consultant.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you can, just don't quote jobs. Don't do whole jobs because it's not worth it. You know, like, the risk is all on you.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: On a fixed-price engagement an erratum in a chosen silicon device is absorbed entirely by the consultant, since the extra debugging effort is unbillable and the payment is all-or-nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: if there's a silicon bug in the chip, right, that can really ruin your day
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Mature, widely used toolchains carry lower latent-defect risk than new parts: far more engineers exercise a mainstream C++ compiler than a newly released embedded device, so defects surface and are fixed earlier.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a lot more people using, you know, the Microsoft C++ compiler than there are people using some little embedded
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Independent consultants do not escape having a boss; each active client functions as one, so three concurrent engagements mean three sets of expectations and priorities to satisfy.
claims.quote_verbatim: Your boss is your client that you're working for at the moment. If you've got three jobs on at once, well, you've got three bosses.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Open online bidding marketplaces for engineering work are dominated on price by offshore consulting companies, which routinely underbid individual local consultants.
claims.quote_verbatim: Oh, like consulting companies out there. They will outbid you every time.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Leaving your name in schematic comments or on production test fixtures makes an engineer traceable years after departure, and former employers use that plus professional networking sites to recruit them back as paid consultants.
claims.quote_verbatim: You leave your name in comments or on a schematic, like a production test fixture, you can guarantee they will track you down.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mars, Makerbot & Power Outages - Reprobate Replicator Replication

claims.claim_text: Naming a one-person consultancy something other than the founder's own name is a deliberate positioning choice, though buyers scanning vendor listings can usually still tell an individual from a multi-person firm.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's very easy to tell when it's a person versus, you know, a consulting company
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Chip and software vendors publish lists of contractors competent in their tools or programs, and entry is typically by application; such listings are a lead channel that clients actively search when looking for a consultant.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of like chip vendors or software vendors will, you know, list people who are competent in their programs or whatever. And it's usually just an application process.
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Measured per hour, writing a technical book returns far less than consulting at the same author's rates; its value lies in doors opened rather than royalties, and one author traced an entire subsequent hardware company to the book.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would have been better off spending that time doing consulting work or working on the business
claims.speaker: Jonathan Oxer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jon Oxer - Innoxious Implant Innovator

claims.claim_text: Long-term consulting business is sustained by repeat work and referrals rather than by maximising each invoice, so experienced consultants absorb small items such as a ten-minute clarifying phone call rather than billing them.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you do a good job for people, they will come back for more and they will refer you.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: Customer-supplied requirement documents are rarely complete or usable, so the standard opening step of an engagement is for the consultant to write a specification back to the customer stating what they believe the requirements are.
claims.quote_verbatim: I then send them a spec on what I think their requirements are because, I mean, I've never, ever seen a spec document from a customer that's been anything like complete enough or usable.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: Running several small jobs concurrently is only workable if customers have been trained not to expect unrealistic timescales; with realistic delivery dates agreed up front, a consultant can multiplex engagements.
claims.quote_verbatim: you train your customers to not to expect things on a stupid timescale. And, you know, you'd be realistic about delivery dates and you can generally like multiplex the jobs reasonably well.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: Being a client's sole electronics resource creates an implicit duty of availability that constrains a consultant's ability to decline or defer that client's work.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lot of my customers, I've basically been their only electronic resource, which to some extent imposes a certain amount of almost duty
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: An hourly consulting business is fundamentally the sale of the practitioner's own time, which caps revenue at hours available multiplied by rate.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're basically selling your hourly rate, right? You're charging your hourly rate and you're a gun for hire.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Davidson - Hoodied HP Hijinks

claims.claim_text: For a small independent hardware engineer, consulting can return more money than selling a self-designed product, because product margins at low volume are extremely thin.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've made more money doing consulting than actually selling products just because product margins are so thin
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: Clients often prefer a local consultant in the same time zone not for sentiment but because escalation is faster and a failing project can be addressed face to face.
claims.quote_verbatim: just because it's just more practical or it may be if you know shit hits the fan then you know you can just go out and talk to them face to face
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: Specialising in a narrow technical area produces a self-reinforcing referral loop: once a group of practitioners in that field know a consultant, they and their competitors keep calling, which is the main engine of repeat business.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're a consultant in one area and a group of people get to know you those same group of people is going to keep calling you and people you know competitors and others just because you get a reputation
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Troubleshooting, PCBs and LEDs - Quaintized Quich Quelling

claims.claim_text: Consulting demand arrives in clusters, with the same class of problem appearing across several unrelated clients in the same year, which lets a consultant anticipate where expertise will be worth developing.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's often the problem of the year. You know, everybody seems to have this problem this year
claims.speaker: Henry Ott
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Henry Ott - Forced FCC Filtering

claims.claim_text: Writing up a recurring client problem where public information is scarce compounds into further work: a short web write-up on mixed-signal grounding led to a commissioned magazine article and then to a paid course.
claims.quote_verbatim: And I realized there was not a lot of good information out on it. So like in the mixed signal, I wrote a little write-up on my web page about it.
claims.speaker: Henry Ott
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Henry Ott - Forced FCC Filtering

claims.claim_text: Isolation is a recognised working condition of solo consulting, and some practitioners deliberately run podcasts through the working day to substitute for ambient office conversation.
claims.quote_verbatim: they listen to podcasts all day to kind of feel like there's office chatter going on
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: A common bootstrapping pattern is to take on roughly twenty hours per week of consulting purely to cover living costs while the remaining time goes to an independent product or research effort.
claims.quote_verbatim: I picked up consulting like, you know, 20 hours a week or something to actually pay for food
claims.speaker: Scott Driscoll
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: Engineers frequently absorb responsibility for failing projects that belongs to management; at one firm the entire engineering staff resigned after one or two years of 80-hour weeks and heavy travel when it became clear that effort could not compensate for repeated bad decisions above them.
claims.quote_verbatim: they killed themselves. They, they were doing 80 hour weeks, traveling all over and everything. And then they're like, it doesn't matter how hard I work if the wrong decisions keep being made.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Scott Driscoll - Impacable Interdisciplinary Inventor

claims.claim_text: A lower-risk route out of employment is to leave only once an independent recurring revenue stream plus a visible consulting pipeline already exist, with the runway limit understood in advance.
claims.quote_verbatim: enough people signed up for Contextual Electronics that is doing well enough that I feel confident, you know, about it. And some consulting work in the pipeline
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Chris Becomes Self Employed - Quixotic Quitting Quaere

claims.claim_text: Clients commonly assume a consultant will handle everything around the technical task, and consultants who possess only technical skills and execute exactly what they are told leave such clients exposed.
claims.quote_verbatim: They have the good technical skills, but they don't, all they do is what they're told.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Elecia White - Wirewove Worshipping Wookieist?

claims.claim_text: For technical authors the book itself is a loss-making project at contracting rates; its economic function is credibility that generates teaching engagements, with one embedded-systems author deriving about 90 percent of income from teaching rather than consulting.
claims.quote_verbatim: he does a little bit of consulting, but 90% of his, his, uh, income is due to teaching
claims.speaker: Elecia White
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Elecia White - Wirewove Worshipping Wookieist?

claims.claim_text: Engineering consultants price work either as an hourly rate or as a fixed bid, and the hourly rate is treated as negotiable, often set lower where the consultant has less prior experience in the specific subject area.
claims.quote_verbatim: consulting engineers often try and do between, you know, hourly rates or fixed bids, right? And usually the hourly rate is always negotiable
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Cheap Respins And A Time Machine - Multiscience Mercenary Marketplace

claims.claim_text: The billing model changes client expectations as much as it changes risk: hourly billing carries an implied obligation of speed and efficiency, while a job price shifts the client to a it-is-done-when-it-is-done posture.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're charging an hourly rate, people expect you to be more efficient than if you're charging a job rate.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Cheap Respins And A Time Machine - Multiscience Mercenary Marketplace

claims.claim_text: Some consultants move well-understood work onto fixed bids to remove the self-monitoring burden of hourly billing, where any lapse in full concentration during a task such as PCB layout produces guilt about the clock.
claims.quote_verbatim: So, he started bidding, you know, known jobs to the fixed bid because of that, right?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Cheap Respins And A Time Machine - Multiscience Mercenary Marketplace

claims.claim_text: A repeated client request is the signal to productise a consultancy: when many clients ask for the same building block, a standard module can be sold to those who can afford neither the consultant's hours nor a fully custom design.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're going to have people coming to you a lot and be like, I want a Bluetooth device. I want a Bluetooth device.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: Running products and consulting together can be mutually reinforcing when the product line serves the same niche as the client work, which is a reason to retain the services arm rather than exit it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the products kind of benefit the consulting customers so well that, you know, it makes sense to do both
claims.speaker: Colin Karpfinger
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Colin Karpfinger - Blendling Bean Brio

claims.claim_text: A pure consulting business has only two scaling levers, working more hours or charging more, and both are bounded, which is the standard argument for adding developed products alongside client work.
claims.quote_verbatim: the only way you can really scale if you're just doing consulting type work is either work longer hours or charge more. And there's limits to both of those.
claims.speaker: Bob Davidson
claims.episode_title: Impedance Matching" with Davidson and Vandenbout - Presbytes Pushing Portfolios

claims.claim_text: Formally agreed reduced-hours arrangements inside companies are frequently penalised at performance review, with employees marked down for not matching full-time colleagues despite the agreement.
claims.quote_verbatim: they would actually rate them down, even though they agreed to it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Moving from salaried employment to consulting is described as roughly tripling the headline rate while gaining control over which hours are worked, which is the trade offered in place of negotiated part-time employment.
claims.quote_verbatim: And that's when you become a consultant, you triple your rate, and you work whenever you want to.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consulting revenue that arrives as intermittent capital injections can slow a product business, because each new client payment removes the urgency that forces the product forward.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like that drip feed of, like, hey, we got some more capital to keep you afloat

claims.claim_text: Funding a hardware product company out of consulting revenue is a well-trodden path, followed among others by the founders of Punch Through and of Saleae in their early years.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just talked to Colin from Punch Through, the Lightbloom Bean Makers, and he was talking about that. And I think Mark and Joe did that for Salier when they were getting started as well
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Declining an unsuitable enquiry outright is cheaper than engaging with it, because once a prospect is given any opening they will negotiate and consume unbillable time.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's like, because they will engage you and then they'll try and negotiate or do whatever. Once you give them. No. They'll just waste. Piss away your time.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A solo consultant's throughput ceiling is headcount, and work is routinely turned away not for lack of interest but for lack of people to execute it.
claims.quote_verbatim: there is work that I turn down just because I don't have enough people to do it
claims.speaker: Dmitry Nedospasov

claims.claim_text: Early consulting income is lumpy, with jobs appearing and then disappearing, and a large share of early effort goes into finding work, establishing a name and identifying which clients value what is on offer; willingness to do sales is a precondition for going independent.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're not ready to do sales, stay in your cubicle
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Converting a former employer or past colleague into a first client is the ideal launch for a consultancy but is not reliably available; more than one consultant has attempted it on leaving a job and failed.
claims.quote_verbatim: I suppose you could always just like figure out a way to take a client or take somebody that you've worked with in the past and have them become your first client. And that'd be awesome too, but I didn't have that.
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Deep single-topic specialists inside companies are structurally exposed, because the role disappears when that specialty is no longer required or can be sourced more cheaply, which is one argument for holding expertise as an independent rather than an employee.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are super experts at this one thing. And basically when that one thing is not needed anymore, or when they think they can, you know, uh, get it cheaper somewhere else.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Bidding on open contractor marketplaces yields worse work than inbound enquiries generated by a known name, and the most effective way to build that name is to publish your own projects publicly until clients approach you.
claims.quote_verbatim: And I think the best way to do that is to be building your own projects at first, publishing those online
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Once inbound demand exceeds capacity a consultant can select only paid engagements, and unpaid work should never be accepted.
claims.quote_verbatim: Never take a job that's unpaid.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Chronic underpricing is a specific form of undervaluing one's work among consultants, and in practice rates are raised only when demand physically exceeds available hours rather than on any deliberate schedule.
claims.quote_verbatim: the only time that he ever raises his rates, uh, is when he just has too much work
claims.speaker: Jon Oxer

claims.claim_text: The demand signal that forces a rate rise is concrete: requests amounting to about 80 hours of time against roughly 40 billable hours available, which itself represents around 60 hours of actual work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I got people asking for 80 hours of my time. I've only got 40 billable, you know, like that's probably still 60 hours of work.
claims.speaker: Jon Oxer

claims.claim_text: The non-technical skills a new consultant must acquire include how to pitch for work and how to report completed work back to a client, and these are typically learned from practitioners already doing it rather than from technical training.
claims.quote_verbatim: how you go about pitching for work and how you, you know, how you report your work back to them
claims.speaker: Jon Oxer

claims.claim_text: Companies attached to maker and developer communities monetise that reach by selling consulting services around the community's hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: Dragon makes money by offering consulting services effectively

claims.claim_text: Quoting a deliberately high deterrent price is a failure mode as well as a filter, because a client may accept and the consultant is then committed to work they did not want.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes like you can set your price to like the point where you say, oh, well, I'll do it for. Yeah. And then you go, oh shit, I didn't really want that job.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Hardware sold into a technical workflow is often bundled with consulting on its use, so the offering is a package of device plus the expertise to apply it rather than the device alone.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a certain level of like, consulting on top of it or whatever, right? You're selling a package.

claims.claim_text: Absence of a formal degree closes some salaried routes while leaving consulting open, so several self-taught engineers have used independent work as the route into technical careers that employers would not offer them.
claims.quote_verbatim: the lack of degree sometimes prevented certain jobs from happening or like from certain opportunities. But at the same time, then, then that was the hack that was needed

claims.claim_text: Selling a solution to a defined problem earns more than selling hours, so pricing by outcome rather than by estimated effort is the higher-yield structure available to a consultant.
claims.quote_verbatim: you'll never make, you'll never make as much money as a consultant as you will when you're, like, offering a solution to a problem
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An hours-based hardware bid is typically framed as an estimated hour count at a stated rate, for example forty hours at one hundred dollars per hour, with the fixed job bid as the alternative structure.
claims.quote_verbatim: this will be estimated 40 hours at 100 bucks an hour
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Calling an experienced practitioner for advice before accepting an unfamiliar job is a low-cost way to de-risk it, distinct from asking permission to take the work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I called Mike up. Before I even took on the job.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: General consulting advice for installation-scale work is to plan for every contingency, layering backup plans at the design level rather than only on the day of installation, for instance ensuring that half the light strings still function if the rest fail.
claims.quote_verbatim: At least I can get half the leads working.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A first fixed-bid job by a new consultant overran the quoted hours by a factor of 2.5, illustrating that estimation error on unfamiliar work falls entirely on the consultant under a fixed price.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well. I quoted. X number of hours. And it was 2.5 X those number of hours. And it was a fixed bid.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The business skills a new consultant has to acquire in parallel with the technical work are quoting, client management, deciding what is and is not billable, and accounting and invoicing.
claims.quote_verbatim: figure out. You know. Client management. What you bill for. What you don't bill for. Actually accounting and billing.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Under a fixed price the consultant eats every extra hour when things go wrong, and clients apply incremental scope pressure with small changes that a written contract does not fully prevent because refusing each one damages the relationship.
claims.quote_verbatim: They go. Oh look. It's just a little change. And you know. You don't want to be a dick.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Time lost to defects in a consultant's own development tools is not chargeable to the client, who treats the toolchain as the consultant's problem, so tool risk is an unpriced cost of the engagement.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't go to the client and say. Hey. My development tool I'm using. You know. Has this bug.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Under a fixed bid the effective hourly rate falls monotonically with hours spent, so on a five thousand dollar job the consultant's realised rate is determined by how well everything goes.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're charging 5k to get something done. And the more hours it takes. The. The. The less you make per hour kind of thing.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Sourcing new clients, rather than doing the work, is repeatedly named as the hard part of consulting; most leads arrive by word of mouth and few consultants do any promotional work showing what they have built and how they operate.
claims.quote_verbatim: But the other one is just. Sourcing new clients. And. You know. A lot of them are word of mouth.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consultants become pigeonholed because risk aversion is rational for them: given a choice they take work resembling jobs already completed over unfamiliar work that looks more interesting.
claims.quote_verbatim: ultimately as a consultant, you don't like risk. You like doing what you've done before.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: One common structure is a single company that both develops the owner's own products and sells consulting services, offering either complete device development packages or project-based work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I own OneBitSquared, and it is mostly my main business, is actually developing stuff for my own company, but I do provide consulting services through that same company too.
claims.speaker: Piotr Esden-Tempski

claims.claim_text: The alternative structure keeps the two lines separate: a consultancy of about ten years' standing may run a product line with almost no crossover between the product customers and the consulting clients.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've been doing consulting for, I think, about 10 years. And then I have some products too. In my case, the products and the consulting have been almost completely separate.
claims.speaker: Eric Thompson

claims.claim_text: Consulting rates look high to clients who compare them to salaries because they omit what the client is not paying for: insurance, benefits, and the obligation of continued employment, since a consultant can be released immediately.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's like, but you are not, uh, paying, uh, insurance. You are not, uh, obligated to have them employed and not being able to fire them like overnight
claims.speaker: Piotr Esden-Tempski

claims.claim_text: Capital equipment failure is an immediate, unbudgeted cost for an independent: with no employer to supply a replacement, a failed laptop had to be replaced the same day at around one thousand dollars to keep working.
claims.quote_verbatim: I didn't have an employer, so I had to go find a, you know, thousand dollar laptop to that same day
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Starting a consultancy young lowers the required income floor; one practitioner took several years across two ventures before earning reasonable money and credits the ability to run lean during that period.
claims.quote_verbatim: it took me, between Blue Stamp and Young Sirius Designs, it took a few years before I was making reasonable money. And being able to run lean for a few years was certainly helpful.
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: The largest reported shock on leaving employment for consulting is not the loss of the paycheque but the loss of colleague camaraderie and the ability to talk a problem through informally over lunch.
claims.quote_verbatim: the biggest shock, I think, for me was the loss of that camaraderie with the coworkers
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Reaching forty billable hours in a week is rare in practice; sustaining that level implies about sixty hours of actual work, since roughly fifty percent additional unbilled time is needed to keep on top of everything else.
claims.quote_verbatim: I found that reaching like 40 hours of build a week is like, happens very rarely for me to tell you the truth. Um, and 60 hours, actual work. Yeah, it takes, you got another 50% on top of that to keep on top of everything.
claims.speaker: Eric Thompson

claims.claim_text: Weeks with zero billable hours are a normal feature of consulting rather than a sign of failure, and experienced consultants stop reacting to them after enough cycles of forty to sixty hour billable weeks.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used to flip out about those two, but to be honest, once you have the, the 40 or 50 hour or 60 hour billable week
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Established electronics consultants commonly run at least one revenue line besides client work, such as products, a seasonal engineering programme or a paid course, which raises the probability of covering income in any given period.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think all of us have different businesses than just consulting, which is another interesting thing.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Proposals should carry an explicit known-risks section, and the consultant should state up front that a particular task has never been done before and may fail; a good client accepts that framing and proceeds.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have to communicate it to the client and not be afraid of admitting. It's like, I have never done that before. I might fail. Are you okay with that?
claims.speaker: Piotr Esden-Tempski

claims.claim_text: Over a ten-year horizon consulting income does not automatically beat the salaried alternative; one consultant calculated that accepting a contract-to-staff offer a decade earlier, even without raises, would have left him about the same or better off.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I'd have taken that job and, and not gotten a raise, I, over the last 10 years, I probably would have been about the same place or, or better off
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: The recommended cash runway before starting a consultancy is around twelve months of expenses, adjusted for household circumstances since a partner's full-time income materially reduces the buffer a solo consultant would need.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think, I think usually I try to say a 12 months.
claims.speaker: Eric Thompson

claims.claim_text: The recommended first step toward consulting is not technical but financial: clearing debt and putting personal finances in order before starting, because that is what carries the practitioner through lean periods.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of the first steps is to get your personal finance stuff in order
claims.speaker: Eric Thompson

claims.claim_text: The security advantage of employment is partly illusory, since whole engineering divisions were eliminated during the 2008 financial crisis and employees could arrive to find the job gone.
claims.quote_verbatim: you and I were working at Keithley through the whole downturn of the financial crisis. Like you can show up the next day and your job's gone.
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Taking a holiday as a consultant requires an explicit policy decided in advance: whether to go completely dark, what is communicated to clients, whether calls are answered, and what counts as an emergency.
claims.quote_verbatim: do you completely go dark? Do you ask around? You know, like, do you tell your... Obviously, you tell your clients, but do you answer the phone? And what's an emergency?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Contract engineering placements are largely brokered through larger firms, which is a different commercial arrangement from being engaged directly as a named subject-matter expert.
claims.quote_verbatim: But I think contract engineering, you're absolutely right. It's mostly larger firms that are doing that.
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: One working distinction holds that contracting is doing the implementation work while consulting is planning with managers, doing architecture without implementation, mentoring and running reviews; the terms are otherwise used interchangeably.
claims.quote_verbatim: contracting is where you do the implementation and the work. Consulting is where you usually work more with the managers to create a plan that somebody else implements.
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: A recurring failure mode in advisory engagements is being given incomplete information about the situation, so that considerable time is spent producing recommendations that do not make sense against the real constraints.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes you come into a situation and you don't get all the information you should. And so you spend a lot of time consulting for things that don't make sense.
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: Consulting exposes an engineer to a wider range of problems than a single full-time role, which counters the skill stagnation that follows from repeating one class of design; the cost is having to learn unfamiliar domains quickly on a client's schedule.
claims.quote_verbatim: you might find that you still feel like you're not learning anything or your skills are stagnating because you're doing one kind of design over and over again
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Some companies deliberately refuse to contract out particular work, such as core algorithm development, because they want that capability retained in house, which closes off those engagements to consultants.
claims.quote_verbatim: They didn't want contract because they wanted to develop algorithms in-house.
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: Bookkeeping consumes enough of an independent engineer's time that a bookkeeper is recommended among the first five hires of a growing consultancy.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think the bookkeeper is one of the first five people you've hired because it does take up so much of your time if, if you want to do something other than play with QuickBooks.
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: At one-off and low volumes engineering effort dominates the bill of materials: a device with roughly one hundred dollars of parts can require about five thousand dollars of engineering time to reach working condition, though the second unit then costs only the materials.
claims.quote_verbatim: that thing's going to cost, you know, a hundred bucks to make, but it's going to cost you $5,000 for all of my time to get it to the point of working
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Fast-growing companies hire consultants to work on site, which can mean relocation and effectively functioning as staff while remaining independent.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was a great gig consulting onsite for a fast growing company
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: A workable test of professional-level competence in a discipline is whether someone would be engaged as a paid consultant specifically for that one piece of knowledge, rather than whether they have completed one or two successful projects.
claims.quote_verbatim: would you call them up specifically for that one piece of knowledge that alone? That's like when it's a professional.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Years spent as an applications engineer managing customer relationships, including delivering the news that a requirement cannot be met while preserving the long-term relationship, is described as good grounding for later consultancy work.
claims.quote_verbatim: that was a good grounding moving later on into a consultancy role
claims.speaker: Kieran O'Leary

claims.claim_text: Where a design engineer inside a company can escalate through distributor representatives, field applications engineers and factory applications teams, an independent consultant reaches the end of that chain and must resolve the problem themselves.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's always someone up the chain I can talk to
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consulting work has kept small product companies solvent for years, but every engineer assigned to client work is taken off the company's own product, which is the standing tension in a mixed business.
claims.quote_verbatim: if we take people off to do like consulting work, uh, which we have done a lot of, cause again, it kind of kept us afloat for a number of years. Um, you know, it takes away from our own product.
claims.speaker: Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: The US contract manufacturing landscape splits between shops built around ISO and aerospace or military quality standards and smaller maker-oriented shops without such certification; competing as a general contract manufacturer means fighting on pennies, and volume production tends to move offshore regardless.
claims.quote_verbatim: do we want to be a CM where you're fighting for every little penny? Um, and once the volumes get up, it's just going to go overseas anyway.
claims.speaker: Ken Burns

claims.claim_text: A semi-private, application-gated peer forum for consultants exists so that practitioners will discuss client and pricing details they would not post publicly, while making repeatedly asked questions searchable.
claims.quote_verbatim: why not make it kind of searchable, but still private enough that people feel comfortable discussing some detail
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Community advice differs in kind from individual advice: it returns contradictory experiences, and its value lies in the cases where independent accounts reinforce each other, which is the signal that a pattern is real.
claims.quote_verbatim: Well, community help is a different kind of help than focused individual help. You get a lot of experiences that can contradict each other, but if you get kind of reinforcing opinions, it's like, okay, that's probably meaningful.
claims.speaker: Christopher White

claims.claim_text: In a downturn when companies move to cash and liquidate, part-time consulting in the sectors that expand is a hedge available to engineers whose main work has contracted.
claims.quote_verbatim: maybe consult on the side or do some, some small stuff
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: When consulting hours are expensive, paying premium fees for fast PCB and mechanical prototype turns is the cheaper option overall: a five-day turn instead of a three-week turn removes consultant hours spent waiting and aligns with clients whose priority is time to market.
claims.quote_verbatim: it made the most sense to, to like turn PCBs as quick as possible and turn mechanical prototypes as quickly as possible, because that was going to be fewer of our hours and fewer, fewer hours overall
claims.speaker: Kerry Scharfglass

claims.claim_text: At a small, selectively staffed consultancy the individual engineers, not a manager, are expected to hold the schedule and cost conversations with the client and to be present when those decisions are made.
claims.quote_verbatim: the expectation was certainly that individual engineers would would have those conversations with clients as well
claims.speaker: Kerry Scharfglass

claims.claim_text: Every new client has to be convinced afresh that the consultant is worth the fee, and one deliberate technique is recounting selected past war stories in informal settings to demonstrate relevant expertise.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've certainly had lunches and stuff with clients where I was very intentional about telling like strategic war stories in order to encourage them that I did in fact know what I was doing
claims.speaker: Kerry Scharfglass

claims.claim_text: Compared with employment, independent consulting raises both the upside and the downside of the same career, and the practitioner either accepts that variance or should not start.
claims.quote_verbatim: the highs are higher and the lows are lower and you either accept that or you don't
claims.speaker: Kieran O'Leary

claims.claim_text: Running a consultancy teaches sales, business development and the cost of sales, so an engineer who later returns to a corporate applications or design role brings back an understanding of the commercial side they did not previously have.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I went back to any of those jobs, I would be so much better at the job now having a much more appreciation of sales and business development and the cost of sales
claims.speaker: Kieran O'Leary

claims.claim_text: Consultants automate the back office rather than doing it manually, using accounting packages such as QuickBooks or Xero and paying a monthly payroll service that files taxes including awkward state filings, because that time is worth more spent on client work or finding clients.
claims.quote_verbatim: So I ended up just trying to automate everything I can. So like even payroll, I, I pay a monthly fee to a service called gusto and that they file all your taxes.

claims.claim_text: Once time carries an explicit hourly value the buy-versus-build calculation changes across the whole business, and paying for software or services becomes rational wherever it frees hours that can be billed.
claims.quote_verbatim: your time is worth X amount per hour and you start looking at everything a lot differently going, well, I should just pay for this service or product and spend my time working on billable hours

claims.claim_text: A consulting rate has to cover self-paid insurance and taxes and additionally the unbilled time that surrounds the work, which is why the headline number sits well above an equivalent salary.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're paying your own insurance or paying your own taxes, but also, you know, charging enough that you can cover those, those warm and fuzzies after the fact

claims.claim_text: One handling of unfamiliar territory on a client's product is to bill a discounted rate, or not bill at all, for the portion of time spent learning, and to charge full rate only for time spent producing.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just give them a discounted rate or I don't bill them for the portion where I'm learning only where I'm producing

claims.claim_text: Client-side cancellation risk is abrupt and largely unmitigable: an engagement running for about a year ended when the owner simply decided to stop paying.
claims.quote_verbatim: the owner was just like me. I don't feel like paying any more money. You guys are done.
claims.speaker: Jared Wolff

claims.claim_text: Because a consultancy sells a fixed stock of time, its only scaling routes are hiring people or becoming markedly more efficient, whereas a product business scales differently by adding automation and staff to something reproducible.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you're a consultant, what you do is you sell your time. You have so much of it. And the only way you scale that business is you don't make more time. You've got to either hire people or get really efficient with what you do.
claims.speaker: Eli Hughes

claims.claim_text: Publishing reference designs against a newly available open platform is a route for a less established consultant to become the recognised implementer for that technology wave, which is worth more than the component discounts such work sometimes attracts.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you publish some designs, usually that's a great way to get your name out and like show that you can interface to this thing
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Depth and AI with Brandon Gilles and Brian Weinstein

claims.claim_text: General freelancer marketplaces such as Upwork, Fiverr and freelancer.com give inconsistent results when subcontracting engineering work: a job posting attracts a wide spread of applicants including unqualified ones, so heavy filtering is required.
claims.quote_verbatim: I haven't been overly successful with the freelancer sites either. So, Upwork, Fiverr, freelancer.com. I've struggled.
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Prior experience managing a team, while not a prerequisite, materially helps a consultant who begins hiring subcontractors.
claims.quote_verbatim: So, I have the advantage of having been a manager for a few years.
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Some engagements should be declined at any price for reputational reasons; an offer of roughly twenty to twenty-five thousand dollars plus travel to validate a purported energy device was refused rather than bid on.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was offered like 20 or 25 grand or something and a trip to Canada. If I would come out and verify this guy's energy device.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Planned extended absences are handled by giving clients around six months of notice and sequencing projects to complete or pause cleanly, with the real reason stated rather than a vague unavailability.
claims.quote_verbatim: I warned my clients about six months ago.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Contracting in the recruitment-agency sense means being placed by an agency and embedded inside a client company for a defined term of roughly six to twelve months to work on one project, which differs structurally from independent consulting.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're hired like, like on a six month or nine month contract or something like that. So you, so you're embedded in a company.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Investments such as making a design modular against part shortages do not pay back for a consultant, because each engagement is a substantially different design every few months and the reuse never accumulates.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're a consultant, as we're talking about here, you're working on vastly different designs from one, you know, every couple of months
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: In the United Kingdom consultants earn considerably more than engineers in salaried positions, whereas the US comparison is complicated because healthcare and similar costs are bundled into employment.
claims.quote_verbatim: In the UK anyway, consultants earn a lot more than, than people who just go to a salary job.
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar

claims.claim_text: A practical signal that an engineer should go independent is doing the technical work they want unpaid in their own time, for example staying up until three in the morning doing PCB design while the paid role has drifted toward marketing.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would be up till three in the morning doing PCB design.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Consulting is attractive partly because it concentrates time on design and reduces exposure to documentation, regulatory work and repetitive testing that many engineers do not enjoy, alongside schedule flexibility.
claims.quote_verbatim: you are doing design all the time. You're not doing so much of the stuff that frankly, I think most engineers don't enjoy doing like writing the documentation and getting the regulation and repeating the test 100 times
claims.speaker: Shrouk El Attar

claims.claim_text: Doubt about being good enough is near-universal among practising consultants, and the work regularly requires learning something new either at the consultant's own expense or, with agreement, on the client's; clients bringing genuinely unsolved problems are considered the best clients.
claims.quote_verbatim: sometimes it's like, I have to go and learn something, you know, on my own, or if the client is willing on their behalf
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A consultant setting up alone typically starts with a very short cash buffer, in one account about two months with no interested customers, which is why the first period is dominated by cash anxiety rather than technical work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've got a buffer of about two months. I have no customer that's interested.
claims.speaker: Remco Stoutjesdijk
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: Early in a consultancy the self-teaching overhead is severe: on work sold as existing expertise, roughly ten hours of self-instruction can be required for every hour invoiced, a ratio that falls as accumulated experience grows.
claims.quote_verbatim: for every hour that you can invoice to a customer, you need to work for 10 hours to actually teach yourself this stuff
claims.speaker: Remco Stoutjesdijk
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: After about five years a consultancy accumulates two distinct buffers: cash to bridge periods without customers, and a reusable library of intellectual property such as DSP algorithms, frameworks and known platforms that makes new work quotable with less risk.
claims.quote_verbatim: I also built up a good library of IP stuff. So DSP algorithms, frameworks, the number of platforms that you know, and can work with.
claims.speaker: Remco Stoutjesdijk
claims.episode_title: High End Audio with Remco Stoutjesdijk

claims.claim_text: Consulting functions as a structural workaround to the management-versus-technical-track problem, because expertise can be rented at a premium for a short run instead of being bought as a permanent hire; engineers have used it to return to technical work from management.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can kind of sell that expertise at a premium and say, I'm short run, you're not hiring me for forever, but you can use my expertise. You can rent my expertise instead of buying it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Systematic relationship maintenance generates consulting work: one engineer used customer relationship management software to schedule contact, deliberately reaching out on people's half-birthdays rather than birthdays so the contact stood out, and attributed jobs to that practice.
claims.quote_verbatim: he said he would reach out every on people's half birthdays instead of on their birthdays. And that like allowed him to keep in touch with people and that allowed him to get jobs.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Client acquisition splits into push and pull: scheduled outbound contact pushes to a list, whereas publishing technical videos and articles pulls prospects toward the consultant, and both have produced paid engagements.
claims.quote_verbatim: you guys push out these, these videos and instead that pulls people to you
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A third-party design review paid for before fabrication generally costs less time than the debugging it prevents, and teams large enough to run internal reviews should make the review plus an explicit test plan a required step.
claims.quote_verbatim: it always comes back to make these things actually take longer than they would have if they just slow down and paid someone to do a design review, get a third party design review
claims.episode_title: Software for Rockets with Charles Aylward

claims.claim_text: Independent consulting removes the organisational guardrails that a company supplies through established process, so responsibility for every check, including elementary ones, rests entirely with the consultant and nobody will ask for the missing step.
claims.quote_verbatim: the thing that I've learned in my consulting career is that there are no guardrails
claims.episode_title: Software for Rockets with Charles Aylward

claims.claim_text: With no colleague to check the work, a consultant must become their own safety net, which extends to learning each new certification or specification from the written standard and its nuances when a project requires it.
claims.quote_verbatim: as a consultant there, by almost definition, there's nobody there to check your work. Right. So you have to become that person that checks your own work.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Self-review has a ceiling that diligence cannot overcome, captured in the mantra that two people working as a team are worth three, because differing perspectives challenge interpretations that a lone reviewer will not question.
claims.quote_verbatim: he kind of has a mantra that two people working in a team are worth three
claims.speaker: Leigh Brady

claims.claim_text: During the semiconductor shortage consultants were uniformly busy because clients needed help redesigning around unavailable parts, and the shortage coincided with a labour market in which hiring a full-time engineer was effectively impossible.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't know any consultants that are hurting for work because everybody needs help in this space
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Part-shortage rework is uncomfortable to bill because the hours restore a design to where it already was rather than adding value, even though no mistake was made by the consultant.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'm billing my clients and I'm not really providing any extra value
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Deep foundational learning, such as building custom logic with no data sheet behind it, is difficult to charge to a client, so part of consulting is unbilled time spent developing capability for one's own account.
claims.quote_verbatim: There is, there is a part of consulting where you have to spend some time banging your head against the wall for your own good.
claims.speaker: Dave Young

claims.claim_text: Process discipline that a client insists on can be repackaged by the consultant as a marketing differentiator when pitching subsequent work.
claims.quote_verbatim: I think of it as a marketing element for me as me as a consultant.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: One documented route to a first client is direct outreach on a professional network after defining a target segment, in this case small and medium embedded and IoT companies, chosen because large companies were judged unapproachable.
claims.quote_verbatim: So basically I start contacting people on LinkedIn and that's the tool I'm using still
claims.speaker: Andrea Longobardi
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: The binding constraint when pitching a new consultancy is absence of a track record rather than the pitch itself, since prospects are being approached constantly and must extend trust without evidence.
claims.quote_verbatim: I mean, it was very much, very harder at the beginning because, well, I mean, we didn't have any track record.
claims.speaker: Andrea Longobardi
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: Consulting suits engineers who change context frequently, because serving successive clients means moving between different problems and technologies by definition rather than as a career flaw.
claims.quote_verbatim: by definition you're jumping work a lot because you're serving different clients and trying a lot of new things
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: Independent consulting at current scale is only feasible because widely available networks and mature technology stacks let a small operator deliver what previously required a company.
claims.quote_verbatim: being a consultant nowadays is only possible because we have access to a pretty good network and pretty good technology stacks too
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: Where a design carries no product differentiation in the component choice, some consultants select parts solely by existing driver support in their chosen framework, declining any device without a Zephyr driver rather than writing one.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't design stuff in if it doesn't have a Zephyr driver personally, just because like, it is not worth it to me.
claims.episode_title: Moving Down The Stack with Scott Williams

claims.claim_text: When asked to take on work that cannot be accepted, pivoting into an advisory role on that project preserves the relationship and the person's access to the expertise without committing to the implementation.
claims.quote_verbatim: I try to pivot to be more like a consultant for that project, other than just saying flat out no.
claims.speaker: Stephen Craig
claims.episode_title: Engineering Careers with Circuit Break & James Lewis

claims.claim_text: Enjoying personal engineering projects does not predict enjoying engineering for a client, and some practitioners find the obligation to build someone else's design a persistent demotivator despite liking the technical work itself.
claims.quote_verbatim: I don't actually enjoy the engineering for somebody else
claims.speaker: Shawn Hymel

claims.claim_text: A stated attraction of design-for-hire is the externally imposed constraint set, since self-directed projects tend to be given constraints that are never realistic enough to force real engineering decisions.
claims.quote_verbatim: The thing I like about design for hire is actually the constraints it places upon you. When I have my own system constraints, like when I'm in charge of constraints, they're never realistic enough.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
